independent_readback_verification.github_readback_method: GitHub contents API fetched independently from the developer machine, base64-decoded and hashed locally; not a re-read of the writer's own buffer.

what_this_proves: The same content projection was independently exported to three enabled destinations and is byte-identical in all of them, which is the multi-destination oracle for SA-404.
SA-401's GitHub private Markdown destination performs a real authorized write into a private repository and the result is externally readable.
SA-403's Obsidian and standard Markdown destinations both write and read back.

single_destination_failure_isolation.method: Requested an export to an unavailable destination (notion, unconfigured) together with a working one (markdown), then compared the canonical row before and after.
single_destination_failure_isolation.verdict: PASS — the unavailable destination is reported explicitly in skipped_destination_ids rather than silently dropped, the healthy destination still completes, and the Canonical Store is untouched. No rollback.

what_this_does_not_prove: SA-402. Notion is unconfigured: it needs a free Integration token plus a shared data_source_id, both of which can only be created in Notion's own UI by the account holder. Recorded as needs_user_action, not PASS.
SA-404 closure. The reconciliation and retry-after-transient-provider-error path was not exercised; the isolation case above uses an unavailable destination, not a destination that fails mid-write.
Any account-level mirror. The exported row is the canary content, because no real account sync has run yet.
